title: Independent evidence for eVTOL certification and service readiness
question: What turns eVTOL demonstrations into certified commercial service?
why_it_matters: Company flight campaigns are useful signals, but commercial service depends on certification, operating approval, vertiports, insurance, local agreements, weather operations, and public trust.
current_support: FTFN now has FAA AAM context, the final powered-lift pilot and operating rule, eight selected eVTOL Integration Pilot Program proposals, an In Review company-reported conforming-aircraft milestone, and an autonomy regulation-to-service pathway and dependency map.
missing_evidence: aircraft type and production certification milestones
executed eIPP agreements, named sites, test plans, flights, and findings
candidate_records: specific FAA type or production certificate
executed eIPP agreement and flight record
next_action: Follow the final operating rule and pilot selections into executed agreements, aircraft and operator approvals, named sites, flights, safety data, local infrastructure, service, and operating outcomes.

named_records: FAA powered-lift pilot certification and operations final rule
FAA eVTOL Integration Pilot Program selections
latest_review.stage_result: The federal operating-rule and pilot-selection layers are now explicit. The gap remains open for aircraft and operator approvals, executed pilot activity, local infrastructure, service, safety performance, and scale.
latest_review.stop_rule: Do not treat a final operating rule, selected proposal, or company test claim as aircraft certification, operator approval, local service, safety performance, or scale.

notes: Phase 55T advances the regulatory and pilot-selection layers while preserving every downstream certification, local-conversion, and operating gate.
